chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad altogether, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you intends that whenever he asks his Lord for something He would give it to him, so he should despair from all the people, and do not have any hope for himself except from Allah, Mighty is His Remembrance. So when Allah, Exalted and Glorious, knows that to be in his heart, never would He ask for anything but it would be given to him. So take account of yourselves before Accounting is taken against you, for on the Day of Judgement there will be fifty pausing stations, with each stop being of the measurement of a thousand years'. Then he recited: 'in a day the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count'.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for God to grant every supplication according to the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual prerequisite for answered supplication: detaching hope from creation to focus solely on God, a state known as 'al-Ya's min al-Nas'. The Imam links this internal sincerity to the rigorous process of self-accounting (Muhasabat al-Nafs) before the final reckoning, emphasizing the gravity of the fifty stations of judgment. The cited verse underscores the subjective perception of time during these intense moments of divine scrutiny.

en.hubeali: H 14556 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Ali Bin Muhammad altogether from Al-Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al-Munkary, from Hafs Bin Gayaas who said:
